### Questions people ask before they come in

The short answers. Anything else, the team will tell you on the phone.

**How do I book an appointment at Halcyon?**

Call +91 77880 91092 or +91 95536 04226 and the team will find you a slot. Bring any recent X-ray, MRI or ultrasound reports — they often save a second visit. You can also send them on WhatsApp before you come in.

**Where is Halcyon Pain Management Centre?**

3rd Floor, KKR Commercial Complex, at Kukatpally Y Junction on Moosapet Road, Hyderabad 500072 — above the Max showroom. It is a few minutes from the KPHB and Moosapet metro stations.

**What are the clinic timings?**

Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 6 pm; closed on Sunday. Appointments are spaced so the wait is short — call +91 77880 91092 for today’s slots.

**What happens on the day of my visit?**

Five steps in one appointment: you arrive and register, the consultant examines you, the painful joint or nerve is scanned by ultrasound in the same room, the findings decide the treatment, and if a procedure is right it is done there and then. Most people are home inside two hours.

**Will the procedure hurt, and will I be put to sleep?**

Procedures are done under local anaesthetic with ultrasound guidance, so you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic and no hospital admission — you walk out the same day.

**Will I need surgery?**

Halcyon is a non-surgical centre — every procedure here is image-guided and done as day care. The one case where a replacement is still the right answer is advanced grade 4 knee arthritis with joint deformity, and you will be told that plainly rather than treated anyway.

**What will treatment cost?**

It depends on the procedure and how many sittings are needed, so the team gives you a clear figure at the consultation — before anything is booked. Call +91 77880 91092 and they can give you a range once they know what you are being treated for.

**Do you accept health insurance?**

That depends on your policy and the procedure. The team can tell you what applies to your case and what paperwork you would need — ask them when you call.

**What should I bring to my first appointment?**

Bring any recent X-ray, MRI, CT or ultrasound reports, a list of the medicines you take, and notes from any earlier treatment for the same pain. Tell the team when you book if you take blood thinners — they need planning before an injection.

**Who are the doctors at Halcyon?**

Dr. Dasyam Pallavi, Consultant – Pain Management (MBBS, DA, FIAPM, CIPS — Fellow of the Indian Academy of Pain Medicine; Certified Interventional Pain Sonologist, World Institute of Pain, USA), assesses you and performs the ultrasound-guided procedures. Dr. PSS Kiran, Consultant Radiologist – Musculoskeletal Imaging & Image Guidance (MBBS, MD Radiodiagnosis, Fellowship in Pain Management), provides musculoskeletal ultrasound evaluation, imaging correlation and image guidance, working with her.

Treatments

##
Four interventional pathways.
Not a scalpel between them.

Lasting pain rarely starts where it hurts. Halcyon finds the source, then
treats it without surgery — every procedure image-guided, under local anaesthetic,
as day care.

- 01 Regenerative Medicine

- 02 Radiofrequency Ablation

- 03 Prolotherapy

- 04 Hydrodissection & Nerve Blocks

### Regenerative Medicine

Growth Factor Concentrate

A small sample of the patient’s own blood is drawn, its growth factors concentrated, and placed under ultrasound exactly where the tissue has worn. The body does the repairing.

It works by prompting the body to repair the tissue rather than by masking the pain, which is why it is used where a structure has worn or torn rather than where a nerve is simply firing. Nothing foreign is introduced — the concentrate comes from a sample taken on the day.
Read the full guide to regenerative medicine

#### Most often used for

- Knee Pain

- Shoulder Pain

- Hip Pain

- Sports Injuries

- Foot & Ankle Pain

- Elbow, Hand & Wrist

### Radiofrequency Ablation

Interrupting the pain signal

A precise current interrupts the nerve carrying the pain signal. For knee pain Halcyon uses the US FDA-cleared COOLIEF cooled RF system.

It is never the first thing done. A diagnostic block has to confirm that the nerve in question is the one carrying the pain before it is treated — in the neck and low back that means a medial branch block first, and radiofrequency only if the block confirms the source.
Read the full guide to radiofrequency ablation

#### Most often used for

- Knee Pain

- Neck Pain

- Cervical Spondylosis

- Low Back Pain

- Trigeminal Neuralgia

### Prolotherapy

Restarting the repair response

A natural irritant is injected into a slack ligament or tendon to restart the body’s own repair response. A short course of small injections, with minimal downtime — some soreness for a day or two is normal.

The aim is a ligament or tendon that holds again rather than one that has simply been quietened, so it suits the slack, overused and partly healed structures — the heel, the Achilles, a knee that gives way — more than it suits a worn joint surface.
Read the full guide to prolotherapy

#### Most often used for

- Foot & Ankle Pain

- Knee Pain

- Sports Injuries

### Nerve Hydrodissection & Nerve Blocks

Freeing and quietening a nerve

Ultrasound-guided fluid separates a trapped nerve from the tissue pressing on it. Relief often begins on the table, and the nerve itself is left intact.

Nerve blocks are the other half of this pathway, and they are used twice over: to treat a nerve that is firing, and to prove where the pain is coming from before anything else is done. A block that settles the pain is the strongest evidence available that the right structure has been found.
Read the full guide to nerve hydrodissection & nerve blocks

#### Most often used for

- Elbow, Hand & Wrist

- Sciatica

- Slipped Disc

- Shoulder Pain

- Low Back Pain

###
The names you will actually hear
on the day of your appointment.

The four pathways above are delivered as specific, named procedures. These
are the ones that come up most often, and what each is for.

-

#### Diagnostic & medial branch blocks

A small block placed on one suspected structure. If the pain settles, that
structure is the source and the treatment follows from it; if it does not, the plan
changes. In the low back and neck especially, this is what stands between a diagnosis
and a guess.

-

#### Epidural & transforaminal injections

Placed under imaging at the level the scan and the block have identified,
aimed at the irritated nerve root rather than at the whole area. This is the usual
answer for sciatica and for a slipped (herniated) disc pressing on a nerve root.

-

#### COOLIEF cooled radiofrequency

The US FDA-cleared cooled RF system Halcyon uses for
knee pain. A water-cooled probe treats a larger volume of tissue than standard RF, so
the genicular nerves can be reached more completely.

-

#### Suprascapular block & hydrodilatation

The shoulder pair. The block quietens the nerve supplying the joint;
hydrodilatation stretches a capsule that has tightened. Usually run alongside a
movement programme, so the range that is freed up is kept.

Which of these you are offered is decided by the scan and the block, not by
a menu — how that decision is made is set
out with the conditions.

###
What none of the four
will ask you to go through.

- No scalpel — every procedure here is image-guided through a needle

- No general anaesthetic — you stay awake and talking throughout

- No hospital admission and no overnight stay

- No second appointment to get the scan read — it is done in the room

#### Where this stops

Halcyon is a non-surgical centre, and there is one case where that is not the right
answer: advanced grade 4 knee arthritis with joint deformity, where a replacement is
still what the joint needs.

You will be told that plainly at the consultation rather than treated anyway. How long
relief lasts also varies with the condition and how worn the joint is — which is
why the diagnostic scan comes first, and why the consultant gives you a realistic answer
for your case rather than a number that fits everyone.

### The scan decides which one.

Book a consultation and the diagnostic ultrasound happens in the same
appointment. Bring any recent X-ray, MRI or scan reports you already have.

Pain conditions

##

generating it first, treat it second. Everything below is done without surgery, under
local anaesthetic, as day care.

###
Every condition treated at Halcyon,
and what is usually done about it.

Filter
All
Spine & neck
Joints
Nerve pain

Showing all 12

-

#### Knee Pain

Osteoarthritis, meniscal tears and ligament pain

The commonest reason people come to Halcyon. Depending on what the scan shows, the answer may be cooled radiofrequency of the genicular nerves, a regenerative injection, or prolotherapy. Advanced grade 4 arthritis with joint deformity is the one case where a replacement is still the right answer — and you will be told that plainly.

COOLIEF cooled RF
Read the full guide to knee pain

-

#### Low Back Pain

Facet joint, disc and sacroiliac pain

Low back pain can come from the facet joints, a disc or the sacroiliac joint, and those need different treatments. A diagnostic block is usually done first to prove which one it is, and the treatment follows from that.

Diagnostic block first
Read the full guide to low back pain

-

#### Neck Pain

Facet joint, disc and muscular neck pain

Neck pain is usually facet joint or disc related. A medial branch block identifies the joint involved, and cervical facet radiofrequency treats it if the block confirms the source.

Medial branch block
Read the full guide to neck pain

-

#### Shoulder Pain

Frozen shoulder and rotator cuff injury

Frozen shoulder and rotator cuff problems are treated with a suprascapular nerve block, hydrodilatation or a regenerative injection, depending on what the ultrasound shows — usually alongside a movement programme, so the range comes back.

Suprascapular block
Read the full guide to shoulder pain

-

#### Sciatica

Leg pain radiating from a compressed nerve root

Pain running from the back into the leg usually means a nerve root is being compressed. Treatment is a transforaminal or epidural injection placed under imaging, aimed at the root that is actually irritated rather than at the whole area.

Transforaminal block
Read the full guide to sciatica

-

#### Slipped Disc

A herniated disc pressing on a nerve root

In most cases a herniated disc is treated with an image-guided epidural injection rather than surgery. The scan and a diagnostic block confirm which level is involved before anything is done.

Epidural injection
Read the full guide to slipped disc

-

#### Hip Pain

Bursitis, labral tears and an arthritic hip

Hip pain from bursitis, a labral tear or an arthritic joint is treated with an image-guided injection into the exact structure involved. The hip sits deep enough that guidance matters more here than almost anywhere else.

Image-guided injection
Read the full guide to hip pain

-

#### Sports Injuries

Tendon, ligament and overuse injury

The injury is scanned to grade the damage, then treated with regenerative therapy or prolotherapy so the tissue heals rather than just quietens down. Return-to-sport timing is planned with you rather than handed to you.

Regenerative therapy
Read the full guide to sports injuries

-

#### Trigeminal Neuralgia

Sudden electric pain across one side of the face

When medication no longer controls the pain, radiofrequency ablation of the affected branch offers lasting relief. It is worth being assessed early — trigeminal neuralgia rarely settles on its own.

Radiofrequency ablation
Read the full guide to trigeminal neuralgia

-

#### Elbow, Hand & Wrist

Tennis elbow, carpal tunnel and de Quervain’s

Usually treated with nerve hydrodissection or a regenerative injection — freeing or repairing the structure rather than releasing it surgically. Ultrasound-guided fluid separates a trapped nerve from the tissue pressing on it, and the nerve itself is left intact.

Nerve hydrodissection
Read the full guide to elbow, hand & wrist

-

#### Foot & Ankle Pain

Plantar fasciitis and Achilles tendinitis

Heel pain that is worst on the first steps of the morning is usually plantar fasciitis; pain behind the ankle is often Achilles tendinitis. Both respond to prolotherapy or a regenerative injection placed under ultrasound.

Prolotherapy
Read the full guide to foot & ankle pain

-

#### Cervical Spondylosis

Age-related wear through the cervical spine

The wear itself shows on almost every scan after a certain age, so the scan alone does not make the diagnosis. A medial branch block is used to prove that the worn facet joints are what is actually hurting, and cervical facet radiofrequency treats them if it does.

Cervical facet RF
Read the full guide to cervical spondylosis

Nothing under that heading — try another part of the body.

###
Two people with the same X-ray
do not always need the same procedure.

01

#### The examination narrows it

The consultant works out which structure is likely to be generating the
pain — which is often not the place you feel it. Referred pain from the back to
the leg, or from the neck to the arm, is the rule rather than the exception.

02

#### The ultrasound confirms it

The suspected joint, tendon or nerve is scanned in the same room. The scan
is used twice: first to find the pain generator, then to guide the needle exactly where
it needs to go.

03

#### A diagnostic block proves it

Where several structures could explain the same pain — the low back
especially — a small diagnostic block is done first to prove which one it is.
The treatment then follows from that answer, not from a guess.

#### Do not wait for an appointment

Sudden weakness in a limb, loss of bladder or bowel control, or back pain with fever
needs to be seen urgently — go to a hospital emergency department now rather than
booking a slot here. If you are not sure, call +91 77880 91092
and ask.

### Not sure which one is yours?

That is what the first appointment is for. Bring any recent X-ray, MRI or
scan reports — they often save a second visit.

Pain Management

### Dr. Dasyam Pallavi

Consultant – Pain Management

MBBS, DA, FIAPM, CIPS — Fellow of the Indian Academy of Pain Medicine;
Certified Interventional Pain Sonologist, World Institute of Pain (WIP), USA.

CIPS is an international certification focused specifically on
ultrasound-guided interventional pain procedures. It is awarded only after the World
Institute of Pain’s structured examination — written, oral and practical,
cadaver-based assessment of anatomy, sonoanatomy and the use of ultrasound during a
procedure — and is held by a comparatively limited group of physicians.

Her clinical work includes ultrasound-guided pain interventions,
musculoskeletal ultrasound, peripheral nerve interventions, radiofrequency procedures,
joint and periarticular interventions, and the management of chronic musculoskeletal pain.

Qualifications MBBS, DA
Regd. No. 61959 — Telangana State Medical Council

Certification & fellowship CIPS — World Institute of Pain (WIP), USA
FIAPM — Indian Academy of Pain Medicine

Clinical interests Ultrasound-guided pain interventions, peripheral nerve and radiofrequency procedures, joint and periarticular interventions

Consults at Kukatpally Y Junction, Hyderabad — by appointment

Book with Dr. Pallavi

See what she treats
Full profile of Dr. Pallavi

Musculoskeletal Imaging

### Dr. PSS Kiran

Consultant Radiologist – Musculoskeletal Imaging & Image Guidance

MBBS, MD (Radiodiagnosis), Fellowship in Pain Management — with
additional training in musculoskeletal ultrasound.

An abnormality on an MRI or X-ray is not always the source of the pain.
Dr. Kiran’s role at Halcyon is the radiological evaluation of musculoskeletal and pain
conditions: reading X-rays, MRI and ultrasound in the context of your symptoms and the
clinical examination, so that what the image shows is weighed against what you feel.

He provides focused musculoskeletal ultrasound evaluation, imaging
correlation and radiological assistance for image-guided pain procedures, in
collaboration with Dr. Dasyam Pallavi — so clinical and imaging information are
considered together as part of an individualised approach to your care.

Qualifications MBBS, MD (Radiodiagnosis)
Regd. No. 62201 — Telangana State Medical Council

Fellowship training Pain Management
Musculoskeletal Ultrasound

Clinical interests Musculoskeletal ultrasound and imaging, peripheral nerve ultrasound, MRI–X-ray–ultrasound correlation, image guidance for pain procedures

Consults at Kukatpally Y Junction, Hyderabad — by appointment

###
However you come in,
the appointment runs the same way.

01

#### No hand-offs

The consultant who examines you is there for the scan, and performs the
procedure if one is indicated — with the imaging read alongside, in the same visit.
Nothing is handed to a separate team, and nothing has to be explained twice.

02

#### The scan decides

Nothing is injected on a hunch. If the ultrasound rules out the structure
the examination suspected, you leave with a different plan — not with a
procedure you did not need.

03

#### Awake, and home the same day

Procedures are done under local anaesthetic as day care. No admission and
no general anaesthetic, so most people are home within about two hours of arriving.

##
A pain centre built around one question:
where is this actually coming from?

the latest interventional techniques at an affordable cost — so that people can
get back to living pain-free lives.

###
A comprehensive pain management centre
in Kukatpally, Hyderabad.

Halcyon treats long-standing pain the way it behaves — as something with
a source that has to be found before it can be treated. Pain that lasts is rarely where it
hurts, so every appointment begins with an examination and a diagnostic ultrasound, and the
treatment follows from what those show.

Nothing here needs a scalpel. Procedures are image-guided, done under local
anaesthetic while you are awake, and you go home the same day.

###
Diagnosis and treatment
in the same appointment.

The consultant who takes your history is the one who scans you, reads the
scan and — when it says a procedure is the right answer — performs it before
you leave. Nothing is handed to a second team, and nothing has to be explained twice.

Appointments are spaced through the day, so the wait is short. Most people
are home inside two hours of arriving.
See the visit in full

Reception takes your details and any scans or reports you have brought with you.

The suspected joint, tendon or nerve is scanned in the same room.

- 1:05 The scan sets the treatment
If an image-guided procedure is right, it is done there and then under local anaesthetic.

- 1:45 You go home
No admission and no general anaesthetic — with aftercare instructions and a review date.

### Finding us

Above the Max showroom at Kukatpally Y Junction, on Moosapet Road — a few minutes from the KPHB and Moosapet metro stations.

### Before you come

Call ahead so the team can give you a slot and tell you roughly how long the visit will take. Most procedures are day care, and you go home the same day.

- Bring any recent X-ray, MRI, CT or ultrasound reports.

- Bring a list of the medicines you take, and notes from any earlier treatment for the same pain.

- If you take blood thinners, say so when you book — they need planning before an injection. Do not stop any medicine on your own.

### Common questions

**Is there parking at the clinic?**

The clinic is in the KKR Commercial Complex at Kukatpally Y Junction. Call the team before you set out and they will tell you where it is easiest to park or be dropped off.

**How do I reach Halcyon by metro?**

The nearest stations are KPHB Colony and Moosapet on the Red Line, each a few minutes from Kukatpally Y Junction. The clinic is on the 3rd floor of the KKR Commercial Complex, above the Max showroom on Moosapet Road.

**Can I send my reports before the appointment?**

No referral is needed. Call to book, and bring any reports and prescriptions you already have for the same pain.

## Privacy Policy

How Halcyon Pain Management Centre handles the personal and health
information you give us — and what this website does and does not collect.

Last updated 22 August 2026

### Contents

- Who we are

- What this policy covers

- What this website collects

- Information we collect

- Why we use it

- Your consent

- Who we share it with

- How long we keep it

- How we protect it

- Changes to this policy

- Contact and grievances

#### Draft — not yet reviewed

This policy is a working draft written from what the clinic’s own website says
about its practice. The highlighted phrases are decisions only Halcyon can make, and
the whole document should be checked by a lawyer against the Digital Personal Data
Protection Act, 2023 and the medical records rules that apply in Telangana before it
is published. Delete this box once it has been.

### 1. Who we are

Halcyon Pain Management Centre is a pain management clinic at 3rd Floor, KKR Commercial
Complex, Kukatpally Y Junction, Moosapet Road, Hyderabad, Telangana 500072. In this
policy, “we”, “us” and “Halcyon” mean that clinic,
and “you” means anyone who contacts us, attends an appointment, or uses
this website.

We decide how and why your personal data is handled, which under the Digital Personal
Data Protection Act, 2023 makes us the data fiduciary for it.

### 2. What this policy covers

It covers information you give us when you enquire, book, or attend the clinic, and
anything this website collects. It does not cover other websites we link to —
Google Maps for directions, for instance — which have their own policies.

### 3. What this website collects

Only what you choose to give the assistant when you ask the team to call you back,
and — if you agree to it — anonymous statistics about how the site is used.

The assistant. It answers from a fixed list of answers held in the
website itself; your questions are not sent to anyone while you chat. If you ask for a
call back and press Send to the team , the assistant sends the clinic: the name
and mobile number you give, where the pain is and for how long, which scans you have
had, the time you would like to be called, the questions you asked in the chat, the
page you were on, and how you reached the site (for example, the name of the search or
social media advert you clicked). Nothing is sent until you press that button, and you
can use WhatsApp or call instead.

Where it goes. The request is saved in the clinic’s own Google
Sheet and emailed to the clinic’s own mailbox, using Google Workspace services that
act on the clinic’s behalf. It is used only to call you back about your enquiry
and to understand which pages and adverts bring people to the clinic. It is not sold
or used to advertise to you. Confirm how long call-back requests are
kept before they are deleted .

Stored in your own browser. So the conversation is not lost when you
move between pages, the assistant keeps it in your browser until you close the tab. It
also remembers, for up to 90 days, which page or advert first brought you to the site,
so a later call-back request can say so. This stays on your device; clearing your
browser’s site data removes it.

Cookies and measurement. When you first arrive, we ask whether we
may use cookies to see how the site is used. Nothing is loaded until you press
Accept : no cookies are set, and Google Tag Manager — which we use to
run our website statistics — is not even downloaded. If you accept, it and the
measurement tools it manages may set cookies to count visits, see which pages and
adverts bring people to the site, and spot pages that are not working. If you decline,
or ignore the notice, the site works exactly the same. You can change your mind at any
time: change your cookie choice . Confirm
which measurement tools are switched on inside Tag Manager, and list them here .

Our web host may keep standard server logs of requests, including IP addresses, for
security and troubleshooting. Confirm what your host logs and for
how long .

If advertising pixels, an online booking system or a live chat service are added later
— including through Tag Manager — this section must be updated before they
go live.

### 4. Information we collect

#### When you contact us

- Your name and phone number when you call or message us.

- Your email address if you write to us.

- Anything you choose to send over WhatsApp, including scans, reports and photographs.

#### When you attend the clinic

- Identification and contact details taken at reception.

- Your medical history, symptoms and examination findings.

- Diagnostic ultrasound images taken in the consulting room, and any X-ray, MRI, CT or
other reports you bring or send.

- Details of the procedures performed, medicines used, aftercare given and reviews
attended.

- Payment records. Confirm whether card details are held by the
clinic or only by the payment provider .

Health information of this kind is sensitive. We ask for it only where it is needed to
work out where your pain is coming from and to treat it safely.

### 5. Why we use it

- To answer your enquiry and arrange an appointment.

- To reach a diagnosis, plan treatment, and carry it out safely — including
knowing about blood thinners, diabetes, blood pressure or pregnancy, which change
what can be used.

- To keep an accurate clinical record and to follow up after a procedure.

- To raise and settle bills, and to support an insurance or reimbursement claim where
you ask us to.

- To meet our legal, professional and regulatory obligations as a medical
establishment.

We do not sell your information, and we do not use it for advertising.
Confirm whether appointment reminders or clinic updates are sent,
and how people opt out .

### 6. Your consent

Where we rely on your consent, we ask for it before we take the information, and you
may withdraw it at any time by contacting us. Withdrawing consent does not undo
anything already done with the information, and there are records we must keep even
after you withdraw — a clinical record of a procedure that has been performed,
for example.

Some information we handle for reasons the law allows without separate consent, such as
providing medical treatment in an emergency or complying with a legal requirement.

### 7. Who we share it with

We share your information only where there is a reason to, and only as much as is
needed:

- The consultants and clinical staff treating you.

- Laboratories, imaging centres and other providers involved in your care.
List the ones you use .

- Service providers who work on our behalf — for example the practice management
or record-keeping software we use — under an obligation to keep it
confidential. Name the systems that hold patient data .

### 8. How long we keep it

We keep clinical records for as long as we are required to, and for as long as they may
be needed for your continuing care. Enquiries that do not lead to an appointment are
kept for a shorter period and then deleted.

Set the actual retention periods here — for outpatient records,
for images, for billing records, and for enquiries — against the medical records
rules that apply to you .

### 9. How we protect it

Access to records is limited to the people who need it for your care or for running the
clinic. Paper records are held securely at the clinic and electronic records are held
on describe the systems and their protections — access
control, encryption, backups .

Pain Conditions

## Knee pain treatment in Hyderabad, without surgery

Examined and scanned by ultrasound in one appointment at Kukatpally — and, if a procedure is right, treated there and then under local anaesthetic.

Book an appointment
Common questions

Knee pain is the commonest reason people come to Halcyon in Kukatpally, Hyderabad, and it usually comes from osteoarthritis, a meniscal tear or a strained ligament. The consultant scans the knee with ultrasound in the same appointment and, depending on what it shows, treats it with COOLIEF cooled radiofrequency, a regenerative injection or prolotherapy. Every procedure is done under local anaesthetic as day care, so you go home the same day.

### What is knee pain?

Knee pain is pain arising from any of the structures in and around the knee joint: the cartilage lining the bones, the meniscus, the ligaments, the tendons, or the small nerves that carry pain signals from the joint. It can follow an injury or build up slowly over years.
Where the pain is felt does not always tell you which structure is causing it, which is why the cause needs to be found before anything is treated.

### Common causes of knee pain

Most long-standing knee pain has one of a handful of causes, and more than one can be present in the same knee.
- Osteoarthritis — gradual wear of the cartilage, more common with age, excess weight or an old injury
- Meniscal tears — from a twisting injury, or from wear in an older knee
- Ligament sprains and slackness — a knee that feels loose or gives way
- Tendon problems around the kneecap, often from overuse or sport
- Bursitis — inflammation of a fluid-filled sac near the joint

### Symptoms of knee pain

Symptoms depend on the cause, but these are the ones people describe most often.
- Pain on walking, climbing stairs or getting up from a chair
- Stiffness, especially in the morning or after sitting
- Swelling or a feeling of warmth around the joint
- Clicking, grinding or catching
- A knee that gives way or will not fully bend or straighten

### How Halcyon finds the cause

At Halcyon’s Hyderabad centre the consultant who examines your knee also scans it with diagnostic ultrasound in the same room, so the likely source of the pain is identified in one sitting. Bring any recent X-ray or MRI reports; they add to what the scan shows.
Before radiofrequency is used, a diagnostic block confirms that the genicular nerves are the ones carrying the pain. If the block settles the pain, the treatment follows from that answer rather than from a guess.

### Non-surgical treatment options at Halcyon

The treatment is chosen by what the scan shows, not from a menu. The usual options are:
Halcyon is a non-surgical centre. If you have advanced grade 4 arthritis with joint deformity, a knee replacement may still be the right answer, and you will be told that plainly rather than treated anyway.
- COOLIEF cooled radiofrequency of the genicular nerves — the US FDA-cleared cooled RF system, used to interrupt the pain signal from an arthritic knee
- Regenerative injection — growth factor concentrate from your own blood, placed under ultrasound where the tissue has worn or torn
- Prolotherapy — a natural irritant injected into a slack ligament or tendon to restart its repair, suited to a knee that gives way

### What to expect on the day and after

If a procedure is right for you, it is usually done in the same appointment, under local anaesthetic and ultrasound guidance. You stay awake throughout, there is no general anaesthetic and no admission, and most people are home within about two hours.
Most people walk out and go about a normal day, with aftercare instructions and a review date. After prolotherapy some soreness for a day or two is normal. How long relief lasts varies with the cause and how worn the joint is, so the consultant gives you a realistic answer for your knee.

### When to see a doctor

Book an assessment if knee pain has lasted more than a few weeks, keeps returning, or is limiting walking, sleep or work. Some situations need urgent care at a hospital emergency department instead:
- A hot, red, swollen knee with fever, which can mean infection
- A fall or injury after which you cannot put weight on the leg, or the knee looks deformed
- Swelling, pain and tenderness in the calf, especially after a long journey or surgery

### Treatments used for knee pain

Which one is right is decided by what the scan shows, not chosen in advance.

Radiofrequency Ablation Radiofrequency ablation uses a precise, controlled current to interrupt the nerve that carries a pain signal. Regenerative Medicine Regenerative medicine at Halcyon means a growth factor concentrate made from a small sample of your own blood and placed under ultrasound exactly where a tendon, ligament or joint has worn or torn. Prolotherapy Prolotherapy is an injection treatment in which a natural irritant is placed into a slack or weakened ligament or tendon to restart the body’s own repair response.

### Questions about knee pain

**Can knee pain be treated without surgery?**

In many cases, yes. Depending on what the ultrasound shows, knee pain at Halcyon is treated with cooled radiofrequency of the genicular nerves, a regenerative injection or prolotherapy, all done as day care under local anaesthetic. The exception is advanced grade 4 arthritis with joint deformity, where a replacement may still be the right answer, and you will be told that plainly.

**What is COOLIEF cooled radiofrequency for the knee?**

COOLIEF is the US FDA-cleared cooled radiofrequency system Halcyon uses for knee pain. A water-cooled probe interrupts the genicular nerves that carry pain signals from the joint, and treats a larger volume of tissue than standard radiofrequency, so the nerves can be reached more completely. A diagnostic block is done first to confirm those nerves are the source.

**Is a regenerative injection the same as PRP?**

It works on a similar principle. A small sample of your own blood is drawn on the day, its growth factors are concentrated, and the concentrate is placed under ultrasound exactly where the tissue has worn. It aims to prompt the body to repair the tissue rather than mask the pain, and nothing foreign is introduced.

**Will the procedure hurt?**

Procedures are done under local anaesthetic with ultrasound guidance, so the skin and deeper tissues are numbed first and you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic. Some people feel pressure or brief discomfort, and some soreness afterwards is normal, particularly for a day or two after prolotherapy.

**How long does the relief last?**

That depends on the cause of the pain, how worn the joint is and which treatment is used, so there is no single number that fits everyone. The diagnostic scan comes first for exactly this reason, and the consultant will give you a realistic answer for your own knee at the consultation.

**What should I bring to my knee pain appointment?**

Bring any recent X-ray, MRI, CT or ultrasound reports, a list of the medicines you take and notes from earlier treatment for the same knee. If you take blood thinners, tell the team when you book, because they need planning before an injection. Do not stop any medicine on your own.

Usual procedures COOLIEF cooled RF, regenerative injection or prolotherapy

Guidance Ultrasound-guided

Anaesthesia Local anaesthetic, awake throughout

Hospital stay Day care, home the same day

- Foot & Ankle Pain Heel pain that is worst on the first steps of the morning is usually plantar fasciitis; pain at the back of the ankle is often Achilles tendinitis.

## Low back pain treatment in Hyderabad, without surgery

Examined and scanned by ultrasound in one appointment at Kukatpally — and, if a procedure is right, treated there and then under local anaesthetic.

Book an appointment
Common questions

Low back pain can come from the facet joints, a disc or the sacroiliac joint, and each needs a different treatment. At Halcyon in Kukatpally a diagnostic block is usually done first to prove which one is responsible, and the treatment follows from that answer — radiofrequency of the facet joint nerves, for example, only if a medial branch block confirms them as the source. Procedures are image-guided, under local anaesthetic, as day care.

### What is low back pain?

Low back pain is pain in the lumbar region, the part of the spine between the bottom of the ribs and the top of the buttocks. Most people have it at some point, and a sudden episode often settles within a few weeks with gentle activity.
When it lasts for months or keeps coming back, it is worth finding out exactly which structure is producing it, because several different ones can cause pain in the same place.

### Common causes of low back pain

Long-standing low back pain usually comes from one of three structures, sometimes with muscle strain on top.
- Facet joints — the small paired joints at the back of each spinal level, which can wear with age
- Discs — a worn or herniated disc, which can also press on a nerve root and cause leg pain
- The sacroiliac joint — where the spine meets the pelvis, often felt low on one side
- Muscle and ligament strain, from lifting, posture or a sudden movement

### Symptoms of low back pain

The pattern of pain gives clues to the cause, though it rarely settles the question on its own.
- An ache across the lower back or to one side
- Stiffness after rest, sitting or first thing in the morning
- Pain on bending, twisting or standing up straight
- Pain spreading into the buttock or thigh
- Pain, tingling or numbness running below the knee, which suggests a nerve root is involved

### How Halcyon finds the cause

At Halcyon in Hyderabad the consultant examines you and reviews your X-ray or MRI reports. The scan shows what is worn, but wear appears on many scans, so it does not prove what is hurting.
That is why a small diagnostic block is usually done first on the suspected structure. If the pain settles, that structure is the source and the treatment follows from it; if it does not, the plan changes. In the low back especially, this step is what separates a diagnosis from a guess.

### Non-surgical treatment options at Halcyon

The treatment depends on what the diagnostic block shows. The usual options are:
Keeping active and a suitable exercise programme usually remain part of the plan alongside any procedure.
- Medial branch block — a diagnostic block of the small nerves supplying the facet joints, which also shows whether they are the source
- Facet joint radiofrequency — used only if the medial branch block confirms the facet joints, to interrupt the nerves carrying the pain signal
- Epidural or transforaminal injection — placed under imaging at the level involved when a disc is pressing on a nerve root
- For the sacroiliac joint, a block aimed at that joint, with the next step explained once it has confirmed the source

### What to expect on the day and after

Procedures are image-guided and done under local anaesthetic, so you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic and no hospital admission, and most people are home within about two hours.
Most people go about a normal day afterwards, with aftercare instructions and a review date. How long relief lasts varies with the cause and the individual, so the consultant gives you a realistic answer for your case rather than a single number.

### When to see a doctor

Book an assessment if back pain has lasted more than a few weeks or keeps returning. Do not wait for an appointment — go to a hospital emergency department now — if you have any of the following:
- Loss of bladder or bowel control, or numbness around the genitals or back passage
- Sudden or worsening weakness in a leg
- Back pain with fever, or with unexplained weight loss
- Back pain after a fall or accident

### Treatments used for low back pain

Which one is right is decided by what the scan shows, not chosen in advance.

Nerve Hydrodissection & Nerve Blocks Nerve hydrodissection uses fluid, placed under ultrasound, to separate a trapped nerve from the tissue pressing on it, leaving the nerve itself intact. Radiofrequency Ablation Radiofrequency ablation uses a precise, controlled current to interrupt the nerve that carries a pain signal.

### Questions about low back pain

**Can low back pain be treated without surgery?**

Often, yes. Halcyon is a non-surgical centre, and long-standing low back pain is treated with image-guided procedures done as day care under local anaesthetic. A diagnostic block usually comes first to prove whether the facet joints, a disc or the sacroiliac joint is the source, and the treatment is then aimed at that structure.

**What is a medial branch block?**

A medial branch block is a small injection that temporarily numbs the nerves supplying one or more facet joints in the spine. If your usual pain settles afterwards, the facet joints are very likely the source. It is used as a diagnostic test before radiofrequency, and radiofrequency follows only if the block confirms the source.

**What is radiofrequency ablation for back pain?**

Radiofrequency ablation uses a precise current, delivered through a needle under imaging, to interrupt the small nerves that carry pain signals from the facet joints. At Halcyon it is never the first thing done. It is offered only after a medial branch block has confirmed that those nerves are carrying the pain.

**Do I need an MRI before my appointment?**

Not necessarily. If you already have X-ray, MRI or CT reports, bring them, as they often save a second visit. The consultant will examine you and tell you whether further imaging is needed. Scans show wear, but they do not always show what is hurting, which is why a diagnostic block is often used as well.

**Will I be awake during the procedure?**

Yes. Procedures are done under local anaesthetic with image guidance, so you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic and no hospital admission. Most people walk out and are home within about two hours, with aftercare instructions and a review date.

**When is back pain an emergency?**

Loss of bladder or bowel control, numbness around the genitals or back passage, sudden weakness in a leg, or back pain with fever all need to be seen urgently. Go to a hospital emergency department rather than booking a clinic slot. If you are not sure, call Halcyon on +91 77880 91092 and ask.

## Neck pain treatment in Hyderabad, without surgery

Examined and scanned by ultrasound in one appointment at Kukatpally — and, if a procedure is right, treated there and then under local anaesthetic.

Book an appointment
Common questions

Neck pain is usually related to the facet joints or a disc in the cervical spine. At Halcyon in Hyderabad a medial branch block first identifies the joint involved, and cervical facet radiofrequency treats it only if the block confirms that joint as the source. Procedures are image-guided, under local anaesthetic, as day care, and you go home the same day.

### What is neck pain?

Neck pain is pain arising from the cervical spine — the seven vertebrae in the neck, the discs between them, the small facet joints at the back, and the muscles and ligaments around them. A short bout after sleeping awkwardly or a long day at a screen usually settles by itself.
Pain that lasts for weeks or keeps returning more often comes from a facet joint or a disc, and it is worth finding out which before treating it.

### Common causes of neck pain

Most long-standing neck pain comes from one of the following, and more than one can be present.
- Facet joint pain — wear or strain in the small joints at the back of the neck
- Disc problems — a worn or herniated disc, which can press on a nerve root and cause arm pain
- Cervical spondylosis — age-related wear through the neck
- Muscle strain from posture, long hours at a desk or phone, or stress
- Whiplash after a road accident or sudden jolt

### Symptoms of neck pain

Neck pain can be a dull ache or a sharp pain, constant or brought on by certain movements.
- Stiffness and difficulty turning your head
- Pain spreading to the shoulder blade or top of the shoulder
- Headaches that start at the back of the head
- Pain, tingling or numbness running down the arm into the hand
- Muscle spasm in the neck and upper back

### How Halcyon finds the cause

At Halcyon’s Kukatpally centre the consultant examines your neck and reviews any X-ray or MRI reports you bring. Wear in the cervical spine shows up on most scans after a certain age, so the scan alone cannot prove which joint is hurting.
A medial branch block is used to answer that question. It temporarily numbs the nerves supplying a suspected facet joint; if your usual pain settles, that joint is the source. The treatment then follows from that answer rather than from a guess.

### Non-surgical treatment options at Halcyon

Treatment is aimed at the structure the examination and block have identified. The usual options are:
Posture, regular movement and a suitable exercise programme usually remain part of the plan.
- Medial branch block — confirms the painful facet joint and can ease the pain for a time
- Cervical facet radiofrequency — a precise current interrupts the small nerves carrying the pain signal from that joint, done only if the block has confirmed it
- If a disc pressing on a nerve root is the main problem, the consultant explains the approach for that at the consultation

### What to expect on the day and after

Procedures are image-guided and done under local anaesthetic, so you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic and no admission, and most people are home within about two hours.
Most people go about a normal day afterwards, with aftercare instructions and a review date. How long relief lasts varies with the cause and how worn the joints are, so the consultant gives you a realistic answer for your case.

### When to see a doctor

Book an assessment if neck pain has lasted more than a few weeks, keeps returning or spreads into your arm. Go to a hospital emergency department instead if you have:
- Neck pain after a fall, road accident or other injury
- Sudden or worsening weakness in an arm or leg, or clumsiness of the hands
- Difficulty walking or loss of bladder or bowel control
- Neck pain with fever and a stiff neck, or a sudden severe headache

### Treatments used for neck pain

Which one is right is decided by what the scan shows, not chosen in advance.

Radiofrequency Ablation Radiofrequency ablation uses a precise, controlled current to interrupt the nerve that carries a pain signal. Nerve Hydrodissection & Nerve Blocks Nerve hydrodissection uses fluid, placed under ultrasound, to separate a trapped nerve from the tissue pressing on it, leaving the nerve itself intact.

### Questions about neck pain

**Can neck pain be treated without surgery?**

In many cases, yes. At Halcyon, neck pain from the facet joints is treated with a medial branch block followed, if the block confirms the source, by cervical facet radiofrequency. Both are image-guided, done under local anaesthetic as day care, with no general anaesthetic and no hospital admission. The right option depends on what is actually causing your pain.

**What is cervical facet radiofrequency?**

Cervical facet radiofrequency uses a precise current, delivered through a needle under imaging, to interrupt the small nerves that carry pain signals from a facet joint in the neck. It is never the first step. It is done only after a medial branch block has shown that the joint in question is the one causing the pain.

**Why is a block done before radiofrequency?**

Several structures in the neck can produce the same pain, and wear shows on most scans whether it hurts or not. A medial branch block numbs the nerves to one joint for a short time. If your pain settles, that joint is the source and radiofrequency can be aimed at it; if not, the plan changes.

**Is neck pain the same as cervical spondylosis?**

Not always. Cervical spondylosis means age-related wear in the neck, and it appears on almost every scan after a certain age, including in people without pain. Neck pain can also come from muscle strain or a disc. The examination and a medial branch block help show whether the worn facet joints are really what is hurting.

**Why do I have arm pain with my neck pain?**

Pain, tingling or numbness running down the arm often means a nerve root in the neck is being irritated, for example by a disc or narrowing around the nerve. Facet joints can also refer pain towards the shoulder. The examination sorts out which it is. Sudden or worsening arm weakness needs urgent medical attention.

**What should I bring to my appointment?**

Bring any recent X-ray, MRI or CT reports, a list of the medicines you take and notes from any earlier treatment for your neck. If you take blood thinners, tell the team when you book, since they need planning before an injection. Do not stop any medicine on your own; call +91 77880 91092 and ask.

## Shoulder pain treatment in Hyderabad, without surgery

Examined and scanned by ultrasound in one appointment at Kukatpally — and, if a procedure is right, treated there and then under local anaesthetic.

Book an appointment
Common questions

Most long-standing shoulder pain comes from a frozen shoulder or a rotator cuff problem. At Halcyon in Hyderabad the shoulder is scanned with ultrasound in the same appointment, and depending on what it shows, it is treated with a suprascapular nerve block, hydrodilatation or a regenerative injection — usually alongside a movement programme so the range comes back. Procedures are done under local anaesthetic, as day care.

### What is shoulder pain?

Shoulder pain is pain from the shoulder joint or the tissues around it: the joint capsule, the rotator cuff tendons that move and steady the arm, the bursa that cushions them, and the nerves supplying the joint. Because the shoulder moves so freely, it depends heavily on these soft tissues, and they are where most problems start.
Pain felt in the shoulder can also come from the neck, which is one reason the source is checked first.

### Common causes of shoulder pain

These are the causes seen most often. Frozen shoulder is more common between about 40 and 60 and in people with diabetes.
- Frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis) — the joint capsule tightens and thickens, and movement is lost
- Rotator cuff tendinopathy or tears — from overuse, lifting, a fall or wear with age
- Impingement and bursitis — the tendons or bursa are pinched and inflamed on lifting the arm
- Arthritis of the shoulder joint
- Pain referred from the neck

### Symptoms of shoulder pain

The pattern differs with the cause, but these are the usual complaints.
- Pain lifting the arm overhead or reaching behind your back
- Stiffness and a shrinking range of movement, typical of frozen shoulder
- Pain at night, especially lying on the affected side
- Weakness when raising or turning the arm
- An ache spreading down the outside of the upper arm

### How Halcyon finds the cause

At Halcyon’s Kukatpally centre the consultant examines how your shoulder moves and where it hurts, then scans it with diagnostic ultrasound in the same room. Ultrasound shows the rotator cuff tendons, the bursa and the capsule directly, so a tear, inflamed bursa or tight capsule can usually be told apart in one sitting.
If the neck may be contributing, it is checked as well. Bring any X-ray or MRI reports you already have.

### Non-surgical treatment options at Halcyon

Which option you are offered depends on what the ultrasound shows. The usual ones are:
Whichever is used, it is usually run alongside a movement programme, so that the range of movement freed up is kept.
- Suprascapular nerve block — quietens the main nerve supplying the shoulder joint, easing pain so you can move it
- Hydrodilatation — fluid placed under guidance into the joint to stretch a capsule that has tightened, used for frozen shoulder
- Regenerative injection — growth factor concentrate from your own blood, placed under ultrasound where a tendon has worn or torn

### What to expect on the day and after

If a procedure is right for you, it is usually done in the same appointment, under local anaesthetic and ultrasound guidance. You stay awake throughout, there is no general anaesthetic and no admission, and most people are home within about two hours.
You leave with aftercare instructions, the exercises to start and a review date. Keeping up the movement programme matters as much as the procedure. How quickly the shoulder improves varies with the cause, and the consultant gives you a realistic answer for yours.

### When to see a doctor

Book an assessment if shoulder pain or stiffness has lasted more than a few weeks, disturbs your sleep or stops you lifting your arm. Seek urgent care at a hospital emergency department instead for:
- Sudden left shoulder or arm pain with chest pain, breathlessness or sweating, which can be a heart problem
- A fall or injury after which the shoulder looks deformed or you cannot move the arm
- A hot, swollen, very painful shoulder with fever

### Treatments used for shoulder pain

Which one is right is decided by what the scan shows, not chosen in advance.

Nerve Hydrodissection & Nerve Blocks Nerve hydrodissection uses fluid, placed under ultrasound, to separate a trapped nerve from the tissue pressing on it, leaving the nerve itself intact. Regenerative Medicine Regenerative medicine at Halcyon means a growth factor concentrate made from a small sample of your own blood and placed under ultrasound exactly where a tendon, ligament or joint has worn or torn.

### Questions about shoulder pain

**Can frozen shoulder be treated without surgery?**

Usually, yes. At Halcyon, frozen shoulder is treated with a suprascapular nerve block to ease the pain and hydrodilatation to stretch the tightened joint capsule, done under local anaesthetic as day care. It is run alongside a movement programme, because keeping the shoulder moving is what holds on to the range that has been freed up.

**What is a suprascapular nerve block?**

The suprascapular nerve supplies much of the sensation to the shoulder joint. A suprascapular nerve block places a small injection beside that nerve under ultrasound guidance, quietening the pain signal. With less pain, it becomes easier to move the shoulder and work through the exercise programme that brings back the range.

**What is hydrodilatation?**

Hydrodilatation is a procedure for frozen shoulder in which fluid is placed into the shoulder joint under guidance to stretch a capsule that has tightened. It is done under local anaesthetic, and it is usually followed by a movement programme so that the gain in range is kept rather than lost again.

**How is a rotator cuff problem treated at Halcyon?**

The tendons are scanned with ultrasound to see whether they are inflamed, worn or torn. Where a tendon has worn or partly torn, a regenerative injection of growth factor concentrate from your own blood may be placed under ultrasound at that spot. The choice depends on the scan, and exercises to strengthen the shoulder usually go alongside it.

**Could my shoulder pain be coming from my neck?**

Sometimes. Pain from the neck can be felt over the shoulder and shoulder blade, especially if it comes with neck stiffness or tingling down the arm. The consultant examines both, and the ultrasound shows whether the shoulder tissues themselves are the problem, so the treatment is aimed at the right place.

**Will I be awake during the procedure?**

Yes. Shoulder procedures at Halcyon are done under local anaesthetic with ultrasound guidance, so you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic and no hospital admission. Most people are home within about two hours, with aftercare instructions, exercises and a review date.

Usual procedures Suprascapular nerve block, hydrodilatation or regenerative injection

Guidance Ultrasound-guided

Anaesthesia Local anaesthetic, awake throughout

Hospital stay Day care, home the same day

## Sciatica treatment in Hyderabad, without surgery

Examined and scanned by ultrasound in one appointment at Kukatpally — and, if a procedure is right, treated there and then under local anaesthetic.

Book an appointment
Common questions

Sciatica is pain that runs from the lower back into the leg, and it usually means a nerve root in the spine is being compressed or irritated. At Halcyon in Hyderabad it is treated with a transforaminal or epidural injection placed under imaging, aimed at the root that is actually irritated rather than at the whole area. The procedure is done under local anaesthetic as day care, and you go home the same day.

### What is sciatica?

Sciatica is not a diagnosis in itself but a description: pain following the course of the sciatic nerve, from the lower back or buttock down the back of the leg, sometimes to the foot. It is usually felt in one leg.
It happens when one of the nerve roots that form the sciatic nerve is compressed or inflamed where it leaves the spine. Many episodes ease over some weeks, but pain that persists or is severe deserves assessment.

### Common causes of sciatica

Anything that narrows the space around a lumbar nerve root can cause sciatica. The usual causes are:
- A herniated or bulging disc pressing on the nerve root — the commonest cause
- Spinal stenosis — narrowing of the spinal canal or nerve exits, more common in older adults
- Spondylolisthesis — one vertebra slipping forward on the one below
- Age-related disc wear and bony spurs
- Pregnancy, which can bring on or worsen sciatic pain

### Symptoms of sciatica

The leg pain is often worse than the back pain, and it can change with posture.
- Pain running from the back or buttock down the leg, often below the knee
- Burning, shooting or electric-shock-like pain
- Tingling, pins and needles or numbness in the leg or foot
- Weakness in the leg or foot
- Pain worse on sitting, coughing or sneezing

### How Halcyon finds the cause

At Halcyon’s Kukatpally centre the consultant examines your back and leg to work out which nerve root is involved, since the pattern of pain, numbness and weakness points to a particular level. Bring your MRI or other scan reports; they show where a disc or narrowing is pressing.
Where more than one level could explain the symptoms, a diagnostic block helps prove which root is the source. The treatment then follows from that answer, not from a guess.

### Non-surgical treatment options at Halcyon

The usual treatment for sciatica at Halcyon is an injection placed precisely at the irritated nerve root.
Staying as active as the pain allows, and a suitable exercise programme, usually remain part of the plan. Halcyon is a non-surgical centre; if your examination suggests surgery should be considered, you will be told so.
- Transforaminal injection — placed under imaging at the opening where the irritated root leaves the spine
- Epidural injection — placed under imaging into the epidural space at the level the scan and examination have identified
- Diagnostic nerve block — used where needed to confirm which root is responsible before treatment

### What to expect on the day and after

The injection is image-guided and done under local anaesthetic, so you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic and no admission, and most people are home within about two hours.
You leave with aftercare instructions and a review date. How much and how long the pain eases varies with the cause and how long the nerve has been compressed, so the consultant gives you a realistic answer for your case.

### When to see a doctor

Book an assessment if leg pain has lasted more than a few weeks, is disturbing sleep, or keeps coming back. Some symptoms need urgent attention at a hospital emergency department — do not wait for an appointment if you have:
- Loss of bladder or bowel control, or difficulty passing urine
- Numbness around the genitals, buttocks or back passage
- Sciatica in both legs, or rapidly worsening weakness or foot drop
- Back and leg pain with fever, or after a fall or accident

### Treatments used for sciatica

Which one is right is decided by what the scan shows, not chosen in advance.

Nerve Hydrodissection & Nerve Blocks Nerve hydrodissection uses fluid, placed under ultrasound, to separate a trapped nerve from the tissue pressing on it, leaving the nerve itself intact.

### Questions about sciatica

**Can sciatica be treated without surgery?**

In many cases, yes. Sciatica at Halcyon is usually treated with a transforaminal or epidural injection placed under imaging at the irritated nerve root, done under local anaesthetic as day care. Many people also improve with time and activity. If your symptoms suggest surgery should be considered, for example progressive weakness, you will be told so plainly.

**What is a transforaminal injection?**

A transforaminal injection is placed under imaging at the foramen, the small opening where a nerve root leaves the spine. Because it sits right next to the irritated root, the medicine reaches the place causing the leg pain rather than being spread over the whole area. It is done under local anaesthetic, and you go home the same day.

**What is the difference between sciatica and a slipped disc?**

A slipped (herniated) disc is a structural problem in the spine; sciatica is the leg pain that results when something presses on a lumbar nerve root. A slipped disc is the commonest cause of sciatica, but narrowing of the spinal canal or a slipped vertebra can cause it too. Not every slipped disc causes sciatica.

**Will the injection hurt?**

The skin and deeper tissues are numbed with local anaesthetic first, and the needle is guided by imaging, so most people feel pressure rather than sharp pain. You stay awake and talking throughout, with no general anaesthetic. Some people notice a brief flash of their familiar leg pain as the root is reached.

**How soon will my leg pain improve?**

That varies. Some people notice a change within days, while for others it takes longer, and the result depends on the cause and how long the nerve has been compressed. The consultant will explain what to expect for your case and arrange a review, rather than giving a figure that fits everyone.

**When is sciatica an emergency?**

Loss of bladder or bowel control, numbness around the genitals or back passage, sciatica in both legs, or rapidly worsening leg weakness can mean severe nerve compression. Go to a hospital emergency department straight away rather than booking a clinic slot. If you are unsure, call Halcyon on +91 77880 91092 and ask.

## Slipped disc treatment in Hyderabad, without surgery

Examined and scanned by ultrasound in one appointment at Kukatpally — and, if a procedure is right, treated there and then under local anaesthetic.

Book an appointment
Common questions

A slipped disc, or herniated disc, is one where the soft centre of a spinal disc pushes out and presses on a nerve root. In most cases at Halcyon in Hyderabad it is treated with an image-guided epidural injection rather than surgery, after the scan and a diagnostic block have confirmed which level is involved. The procedure is done under local anaesthetic as day care.

### What is a slipped disc?

The discs between the vertebrae act as cushions, each with a tough outer ring and a softer centre. In a slipped disc the disc does not actually slip; part of the soft centre bulges or pushes through a weak point in the ring. The medical terms are herniated or prolapsed disc.
A herniated disc often causes no symptoms. It becomes a problem when it presses on or inflames a nearby nerve root. Slipped discs are commonest in the lower back, less so in the neck.

### Common causes of a slipped disc

Usually there is no single cause; several factors add up over time.
- Age-related wear, which makes the discs drier and less flexible
- Lifting, bending or twisting, especially with a heavy load
- Repeated strain from work, sport or long hours of sitting
- Excess body weight, which adds load to the lower spine
- Smoking and a family history, both linked with disc problems

### Symptoms of a slipped disc

Symptoms depend on the level of the disc and which nerve root it affects.
- Back pain, or neck pain if the disc is in the neck
- Pain running down the leg (sciatica) or down the arm
- Numbness, tingling or pins and needles in the leg, foot, arm or hand
- Weakness in the muscles supplied by the affected nerve
- Pain worse on sitting, bending, coughing or sneezing

### How Halcyon finds the cause

At Halcyon’s Kukatpally centre the consultant examines you to see which nerve root your symptoms point to, and reviews your MRI or other scan reports. Disc bulges are common on scans, including in people without pain, so the scan has to match the examination.
Where there is doubt, a diagnostic block confirms which level is responsible before anything else is done. The treatment then follows from that answer rather than from a guess.

### Non-surgical treatment options at Halcyon

In most cases, a herniated disc pressing on a nerve root is treated at Halcyon with an injection placed at the level involved, rather than with surgery.
Keeping as active as the pain allows and a suitable exercise programme usually remain part of the plan. Halcyon is a non-surgical centre; if your examination suggests you should see a spinal surgeon, for example because of worsening weakness, you will be told so plainly.
- Epidural injection — placed under imaging at the level the scan and block have identified
- Transforaminal injection — placed under imaging at the exit of the specific irritated nerve root
- Diagnostic block — used first where needed to confirm the level

### What to expect on the day and after

The injection is image-guided and done under local anaesthetic, so you stay awake and talking throughout. There is no general anaesthetic and no hospital admission, and most people are home within about two hours.
You leave with aftercare instructions and a review date. How much and how long the pain eases varies from person to person, so the consultant gives you a realistic answer for your case.

### When to see a doctor

Book an assessment if back or neck pain with leg or arm symptoms has lasted more than a few weeks or keeps returning. Go to a hospital emergency department now, rather than waiting for an appointment, if you have:
- Loss of bladder or bowel control, or numbness around the genitals or back passage
- Weakness in a leg or arm that is getting worse, or foot drop
- Symptoms in both legs, or difficulty walking
- Back pain with fever, or after a fall or accident

### Treatments used for slipped disc

Which one is right is decided by what the scan shows, not chosen in advance.

Nerve Hydrodissection & Nerve Blocks Nerve hydrodissection uses fluid, placed under ultrasound, to separate a trapped nerve from the tissue pressing on it, leaving the nerve itself intact.

### Questions about slipped disc

**Can a slipped disc be treated without surgery?**

In most cases, yes. Many slipped discs settle with time and activity, and when pain persists, Halcyon treats it with an image-guided epidural injection at the level involved, under local anaesthetic as day care. Surgery is usually considered only for severe or worsening nerve problems, and if that applies to you, the consultant will say so.

**What does an epidural injection for a slipped disc do?**

An epidural injection places medicine under imaging into the space around the nerve roots at the level of the herniated disc. The aim is to settle the inflammation of the nerve root that is causing the pain, so that you can move and recover more comfortably. It does not remove the disc bulge itself.

**How do you know which disc is causing my pain?**

The consultant matches your symptoms and examination to the scan, because disc bulges often appear on MRI in people without pain. Where more than one level could explain your symptoms, a diagnostic block is done first to prove which one it is. The treatment is then aimed at that level.

**Does a slipped disc heal on its own?**

Often it improves. The bulging part of the disc can shrink over weeks to months, and many people recover with activity and time. Pain that is severe, lasts beyond a few weeks or comes with weakness should be assessed. Red-flag symptoms such as loss of bladder or bowel control need emergency care.

**Will I need to stay in hospital?**

No. The injection is done as day care under local anaesthetic, with no general anaesthetic and no admission. You stay awake throughout, and most people are home within about two hours. You leave with aftercare instructions and a review date, and the consultant explains what to avoid in the first days.

**What should I bring to my appointment?**

Bring your MRI, CT or X-ray reports, a list of the medicines you take and notes from earlier treatment for your back or neck. If you take blood thinners, tell the team when you book, because they need planning before an injection. Do not stop any medicine on your own; call +91 77880 91092 and ask.

## Hip pain treatment in Hyderabad, without surgery

Examined and scanned by ultrasound in one appointment at Kukatpally — and, if a procedure is right, treated there and then under local anaesthetic.

Book an appointment
Common questions

Hip pain usually comes from one of a few structures — a bursa on the outside of the hip, the labrum inside the joint, the tendons around it, or an arthritic joint surface. At Halcyon the consultant examines you, scans the hip with ultrasound in the same room, and treats the exact structure involved with an image-guided injection. It is done under local anaesthetic as day care, and you go home the same day.

### What is hip pain?

Hip pain is pain felt in or around the hip joint — on the outside of the hip, in the groin, or deep in the buttock. Where you feel it is a useful clue: pain on the outer side of the hip is often from a bursa or tendon, while pain in the groin more often comes from the joint itself.
Not all pain felt at the hip starts there. The low back and the sacroiliac joint can refer pain into the buttock and hip, which is why the source is confirmed before anything is treated.

### Common causes of hip pain

Most hip pain seen at Halcyon comes from wear, overuse or a tear in one of the soft tissues around the joint. The commonest causes are:
- Trochanteric bursitis — an irritated fluid-filled cushion on the outer side of the hip
- Gluteal tendon problems, often seen alongside bursitis
- A labral tear — damage to the rim of cartilage that lines the hip socket
- Osteoarthritis — wear of the joint surface, more common with age
- Pain referred from the low back or sacroiliac joint

### Symptoms of hip pain

Hip problems usually show themselves as pain with weight-bearing and movement. Bursitis often makes it uncomfortable to lie on the affected side at night. A labral tear may cause a catching or clicking feeling in the groin. An arthritic hip tends to be stiff first thing in the morning and makes it harder to put on socks or shoes.
Other common signs include a limp, pain on climbing stairs or getting out of a car, and a reduced range of movement.

### How Halcyon finds the cause

The consultant first examines the hip and the back to narrow down which structure is likely to be causing the pain. The suspected bursa, tendon or joint is then scanned with diagnostic ultrasound in the same room, so you do not need a separate appointment to have the scan read.
The hip sits deep under thick muscle, so guidance matters more here than almost anywhere else in the body. The same ultrasound used to find the problem is used to guide the needle to it. Bring any recent X-ray or MRI reports — they help, particularly for arthritis and labral tears.

### Non-surgical treatment options at Halcyon

Hip pain at Halcyon is treated with an image-guided injection placed into the exact structure involved, rather than into the general area. What is injected depends on what the scan shows.
Where a tendon or the tissue around the joint has worn or torn, a regenerative injection is often used: a small sample of your own blood is drawn, its growth factors concentrated, and the concentrate placed under ultrasound where the tissue has worn. The aim is to prompt the body to repair the tissue rather than simply mask the pain. Your consultant will explain which option suits your hip and why.
- Bursitis and tendon pain — guided injection into the bursa or tendon
- Labral tears — guided injection into the joint
- Arthritic hip — guided injection into the joint, chosen by what the scan shows

### What to expect on the day and after

Assessment, scan and treatment can happen in one appointment. The procedure is done under local anaesthetic, so you stay awake and talking, and there is no general anaesthetic or hospital admission. Most people are home within about two hours.
You will leave with aftercare instructions and a review date. How much rest you need depends on the procedure — the consultant will tell you what to do and what to avoid before you go. Costs are explained at the consultation, before anything is booked.

### When to see a doctor

See a doctor if hip pain lasts more than a few weeks, wakes you at night, or makes you limp. Some hip symptoms need urgent care instead of a clinic appointment.
- A fall or injury after which you cannot bear weight — possible fracture, go to an emergency department
- A hot, swollen, very painful hip with fever
- Sudden weakness in the leg, or loss of bladder or bowel control
- Hip or groin pain with unexplained weight loss

### Treatments used for hip pain

Which one is right is decided by what the scan shows, not chosen in advance.

Regenerative Medicine Regenerative medicine at Halcyon means a growth factor concentrate made from a small sample of your own blood and placed under ultrasound exactly where a tendon, ligament or joint has worn or torn.

### Questions about hip pain

**Can hip pain be treated without surgery?**

Often, yes. Hip pain from bursitis, tendon problems, a labral tear or an arthritic joint can usually be treated at Halcyon with an image-guided injection into the exact structure involved. It is done under local anaesthetic as day care. The consultant scans the hip first and will tell you plainly if your hip needs a different kind of care.

**Why does the injection need ultrasound guidance?**

The hip lies deep under thick muscle, and the bursa, tendons and joint sit close together. Ultrasound lets the consultant see the structure causing your pain and guide the needle to that exact spot, rather than injecting the general area and hoping it spreads to the right place.

**How do I know whether my pain is from the hip or my back?**

It is not always obvious, because the low back and sacroiliac joint often refer pain into the buttock and hip. The consultant examines both, and the hip is scanned in the consulting room. If the source is still unclear, a small diagnostic block can help prove which structure is causing the pain.

**What is trochanteric bursitis?**

It is irritation of a bursa — a small fluid-filled cushion — on the outer side of the hip, often with the gluteal tendons involved. It typically causes pain on the outside of the hip that is worse lying on that side, climbing stairs or walking for long. Ultrasound can show it clearly.

**How long will the relief last?**

That varies with the cause, how worn the joint is and how the tissue responds, which is why the diagnostic scan comes first. The consultant will give you a realistic answer for your hip at the consultation rather than a figure that fits everyone.

**Where is Halcyon and how do I book?**

Halcyon is on the 3rd Floor, KKR Commercial Complex, Kukatpally Y Junction, Moosapet Road, Hyderabad — above the Max showroom and a few minutes from the KPHB and Moosapet metro stations. Call +91 77880 91092, Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 6 pm, and bring any recent X-ray or MRI reports.
